The United Arab Emirates jewel in a crown enchants numerous expatriate who seek vibrant life, which is rewarding. However, further than career aspirations stand the need for a companion and experiencing life along. Fortunately, the spouse visa UAE ensures that you reconnect with your loved one in this lively city.

In this article, we will uncover details regarding the process of sponsoring a spouse visa in Dubai including who is eligible for such an application, remaining steps and necessary documents. We will also delve into essential factors such as costs needed and the estimated processing time, which you can use to traverse this journey successfully.

Spouse Visa Minimum Salary in Dubai, UAE

Before proceeding to the application stage, it is essential to acknowledge that one of the fundaments of sponsoring a spouse visa UAE involves fulfillment with regards to minimum wages.

Financial stability matters! This provision protects your spouse and any dependents demonstrating that you can support them.

In the UAE, male sponsors have to earn at least AED 4000 per month for men and a monthly salary of AED 15,386 in order legally support their spouses.

As a result, the salary requirement is calculated based on your gross income before any deductions. You will need to provide proof of your financial stability through a salary certificate from your employer.

Instead, if the minimum wage is not met displaying financial soundness in other ways such as savings or investments could activate your spouses UAE visa.

But the sponsor should contact an immigration attorney to present them with his rights. In addition to the minimum salary requirement, sponsors must also meet other eligibility criteria, such as:

  • Having a valid residence visa in the United Arab Emirates
  • Providing a valid marriage certificate
  • Providing a medical certificate for their spouse

So applying for the spouse visa in Dubai can be detailed and demanding. Patience is key! Give the GDRFA a minimum of two months to handle your spouse visa UAE application in its entirety.

The following are some additional tips for sponsoring a spouse visa Dubai:
Firstly, begin the application process ahead of time so that you have a considerable amount of time to acquire documents. However, ensure that you are aware of the latest spouse visa UAE requirements through visiting their government website.

Spouse Visa Cost in dubai, UAE

Meeting the eligibility requirements is essential but do not forget financial aspect as well. The spouse visa UAE cost becomes relevant when inviting his or her loved one to Dubai. The fees differ according to your nationality and the visa you are applying for.

The male sponsor incurs a cost of AED 940 for a UAE spouse visa. This fee is due to the GDRFA.

The GDRFA requires the male sponsor to pay AED 1,937.50 as the required amount for a UAE spouse visa.

In addition, apart from the applicant fee, sponsors should be ready to pay visa processing charges. Moreover, every sponsor contributes! Whatever nationality or gender, AED 510 opens the door for visa processing, forming a part of the overall UAE visa fees.

So the visa processing fee is payable at the Immigration Department.
Furthermore, the spouse visa UAE cost varies: For a man, AED 1450 and for woman AED 2447.

To summarize, Dubai’s spouse visa is a cheaper substitute for other countries. This makes it a reasonably moderate choice for expatriates who desire to have their spouses stay with them in the UAE.

Here are some additional tips for saving money on a spouse visa UAE: 
Planning is critical to ensure a hassle-free, pocket friendly travel for the spouse visa  UAE.

Therefore, apply for the visa early! The processing time can take up to two months, and acting proactively saves you the hassle and expense of late application fees.

Next, avoid unnecessary courier costs by submitting your application in person. It is the most straightforward approach, and you will have immediate access to any clarification or support needed.

Want an extra layer of assurance? Consider using a reputable visa service provider. They can guide you through the process, minimizing errors and offering valuable insights. 

Spouse Visa Required Documents in Dubai, UAE

In addition to meeting the eligibility requirements and paying the required fees, sponsors must also provide the following documents to apply for a spouse visa in Dubai: 

  • Sponsor’s and spouses passport copies. The copies of passports must be valid at least six months from the application date.
    • The sponsor’s and the spouse’s passport-sized photographs. The photographs should have been taken during the last half a year and in color.
    • A valid marriage certificate. The birth certificate should be translated into Arabic and authenticated by the UAE authorities.
    • Spouse’s medical certificate. The medical certificate must be signed by a DHA approved doctor in the UAE.
    • Evidence of accommodation for the spouse. This may be a lease, an employer letter or landlord’s one.
    • Financial support for the spouse. This may include salary confirmation, bank statement or any other financial document.

Moreover, submit the papers in Arabic or English. If the documents are not in Arabic, translate them and have them certified by a recognized translator.

However, the application and supporting documents should be submitted by the sponsor to GDRFA. In two months, the GDRFA will process this application and make a decision.

So here are some additional tips for submitting the required documents for a spouse visa UAE:

  • Make sure all the documents are complete and up-to-date.
  • Submit the documents in person at the GDRFA. This will help to ensure that the documents are processed correctly.
  • Keep a copy of all the documents you submit.

Spouse Visa in Dubai, UAE: Sponsorship Requirements

Ready to build a life in Dubai with your loved one? The spouse visa opens the door to a 5-year residency permit, renewable for boundless possibilities. But before the celebrations begin, let’s dive into the crucial requirements for sponsoring the visa.

Eligibility Essentials:

  • UAE Residency: You, the sponsor, must hold a valid UAE residence visa.
  • Valid Passports & Visas: Both you and your spouse need current passports and visas.
  • Marriage Proof: A valid marriage certificate, translated and attested in Arabic, is key.
  • Financial Stability: Minimum monthly salaries are set: AED 4,000 for male sponsors, AED 10,000 for female sponsors. This is based on gross income, before deductions.
  • Meeting the Minimum Salary

 

Don’t fret if your salary falls short. You might still qualify if you can demonstrate additional financial assets, like savings or investments. However, consulting an immigration lawyer to explore your options is highly recommended.

Provide proof of a secure Dubai home for your spouse, such as a rental agreement or employer/landlord letter. Similarly, show financial stability to support your spouse, through salary certificates, bank statements, or other documents. Remember, documents must be in Arabic or translated and attested.

Once you have all the documentation, submit your application and supporting documents to the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA). Expect a response within two months.

Salary limits

Bringing your loved one to Dubai? Fantastic! One key step is understanding the minimum salary requirement, which ensures you can financially support them. No confusion here! Men sponsoring a spouse visa UAE need at least AED 4,000 per month, while women need AED 10,000. This applies to all jobs, public or private.

Remember, the requirement hinges on your gross salary, before deductions. Simply provide a salary certificate from your employer as proof.

Now, what if your salary falls short? Fear not! You can still be eligible using evidence of other financial assets, like savings or investments. However, this path requires expert guidance. Moreover, consult an immigration lawyer to explore your options and navigate the process smoothly.

So, while navigating the salary requirement might seem daunting, remember, it’s simply a stepping stone to welcoming your love into your Dubai life. Prepare well, seek advice if needed, and soon, you’ll be building beautiful memories together in this vibrant city.

Here are some tips for the sponsors:

Firstly, arrange to have the medical checkup done right after issuing the marriage certificate.
Secondly, ensure the doctor licensed by government. An approved list of doctors is also available on the GDRFA website.
Finally, take all the necessary documents to a medical examination. These include the spouse’s passport, visa marriage certificate among other relevant medical records.
By doing these, you can avoid your spouse failing the medical test and not getting a visa to Dubai.
Medical conditions that may result in the spouse being found medically unfit include:

Medical Fitness

Securing a spouse visa in the UAE goes beyond salary checks! Sponsors must actively obtain a medical certificate for their spouse, issued by a government-approved doctor, proving their fitness for entry.

The medical certificate must include the following information:

  • The spouse’s name, date of birth, and passport number
  • The results of a physical examination, including blood tests, chest X-ray, and urinalysis
  • The results of any other tests that the doctor may deem necessary
  • The medical certificate must be valid for at least 10 days from the date of application.

A medical test revealing unfitness to enter the UAE will unfortunately result in visa denial for your spouse. However, they may be able to apply for a waiver if their condition is treatable.

Tips for sponsors:

Firstly, schedule the medical examination as soon as possible after the marriage certificate is issued.

Secondly, make sure the doctor is government-approved. A list of approved doctors can be found on the website of the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA).

Lastly, bring all of the required documentation to the medical examination. This includes the spouse’s passport, visa, marriage certificate, and any other relevant medical records.

By following these tips, you can help ensure that your spouse is able to pass the medical examination and obtain a visa to live in Dubai.

Medical conditions that may result in the spouse being found medically unfit include:

  • Communicable diseases, such as HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and leprosy
  • Mental illness
  • Cancer
  • Severe heart disease or other chronic health conditions

If the spouse is found to have a medical condition that is considered to be a serious risk to public health, they may be required to undergo treatment in the UAE before they are granted a visa.

Spouse Visa Application Process in Dubai, UAE

Dreaming of sharing Dubai with your spouse? The spouse visa offers a 5-year residency permit, renewable for years to come. But navigating the process can be daunting. Fear not! This guide simplifies the steps.

Gathering Documents:

  • Passport copies (both sponsor and spouse)
  • Passport-sized photos (both sponsor and spouse)
  • Valid marriage certificate (translated and attested in Arabic)
  • Spouse’s medical certificate (issued by a UAE-approved doctor)
  • Proof of accommodation for spouse (rental agreement, employer letter, etc.)
  • Proof of financial support for spouse (salary certificate, bank statement, etc.)

Keep in mind that the following guide serves as a base. Applying these steps and keeping yourself updated with the latest knowledge can enhance your chances of sponsoring your spouse for a visa successfully, get him or her home to Dubai.

Spouse Visa Processing Time in Dubai, UAE

A spouse visa in Dubai, UAE has a processing time of two months. Nevertheless, the actual processing time may differ due to different circumstances of the application.

For instance, if the application is clear and correct, then its processing time will be more likely to take less. If the application is incorrect or not entirely completed, it might take some time to process.

Moreover, the GDRFA can also ask for further information or documentation, which will lead to increased processing time.

However, there are a few things that sponsors can do to help reduce the processing time for a spouse visa in Dubai:

  • Start the application process early. This will give you plenty of time to gather the required documentation and make any necessary corrections.
  • Submit a complete and accurate application. This will help ensure that the application is processed quickly and efficiently.
  • Be prepared to provide additional information or documentation if it is requested.

By following these tips, you can help ensure that the processing time for your spouse visa is as short as possible.

What to Do if Your Application is Delayed

If your application is held back, you should get in touch with the GDRFA to learn more about what has happened. The GDRFA is perhaps able to give you more information about the delay and a time when a decision may be made.

You can also think about employing an immigration lawyer who will be responsible for the monitoring of your application and make sure it is being processed as soon as possible.

A spouse visa in Dubai, UAE is a good opportunity for expatriates to take their foreign spouses with them under the invitation of residence. The application process itself is not too complicated, yet you should be well-prepared with the necessary documentation and start the procedure in advance.

Spouse Visa Validity in Dubai, UAE

The spouse visa in Dubai, UAE is a residency permit that allows expatriates to bring their foreign spouses to live with them in the country. Unfold your Dubai adventure! Your spouse visa unlocks five years of shared experiences, renewable for countless more.

The validity period of the spouse visa begins on the date of entry into the UAE. Your spouse’s Dubai residency hinges on a swift move! They must enter the UAE within 60 days of visa issuance.

The spouse visa is renewable for up to five years. To proceed with the renewal of visa in UAE, the sponsor must submit an application to the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA) along with the following documents:

  • A valid passport and visa of the spouse.
  • A valid marriage certificate.
  • A medical certificate for the spouse.
  • Proof of accommodation for the spouse.
  • Proof of financial support for the spouse.
  • The GDRFA will process the renewal application and issue a decision within two months.

Here are some tips for sponsors who are renewing their spouse visa:

  • Start the renewal process early. This will give you plenty of time to gather the required documentation and pay the required fees.
  • Be sure to check the latest UAE spouse visa requirements with the GDRFA website. 
  • If you are not sure if you meet the eligibility criteria, consult with an immigration lawyer. An immigration lawyer can help you understand the visa requirements and ensure that your application is complete and accurate.

FAQs

Who Is Eligible for A Spouse Visa in Dubai, UAE?

UAE residents who have valid residency permits, have sufficient income, can meet the specified salary requirements and provide a proof of their marriage through an attested marriage certificate that’s recognized in UAE are eligible.

How Long Will It Take to Get a Spouse Visa in Dubai, UAE?

Spouse visa processing usually takes 2 to 4 weeks. But it depends on documentation, medical testing, and approvals. If paperwork is incomplete or additional verifications are required, then the process can get delayed.

For How Many Months Is a Spouse Visa Valid in UAE?

It is usually issued for 1, 2, or 3 years, depending on the sponsor’s residency and employer. It can be renewed too.

What Documents Are Required for The Spouse Visa Application in UAE?

You will need:

  • A valid Emirates ID
  • passport copies
  • attested marriage certificate
  • salary certificate
  • labor contract
  • recent photographs
  • tenancy contract
  • utility bills
  • medical fitness test results
  • health insurance

What Is the Cost of Getting a Spouse Visa in UAE?

Spouse visa costs vary. Usually it includes application fees, medical testing, Emirates ID, and insurance charges. Total expenses, however, depend on your emirate and service provider handling the process.

What Is the Minimum Salary Required to Sponsor a Spouse in Dubai?

You need a minimum monthly salary of AED 4,000 or AED 3,000 plus accommodation to sponsor your spouse in Dubai.

Is Medical Testing Mandatory for Spouse Visa Issuance?

Yes, all applicants must undergo a medical fitness test, including screenings for communicable diseases. Only applicants who pass this test are granted a UAE spouse visa.
